sentences.text: Longchengornis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean birds belonging to the family Cathayornithidae.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — measured 11 cm in length, 7.5 cm in hip height, and weighed 20 grams.
It possessed a wide upper arm bone featuring a unique circular depression at the shoulder joint.
The animal had long, slender legs equipped with large, hooked claws, while its hand retained at least two claws.
The species Longchengornis sanyanensis was named and described in 1997 by Hou Lianhai.
Longchengornis lived during the Early Cretaceous Period, approximately 120 million years ago, with a time range estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
Fossils of this bird have been found in the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning province, China.
Some researchers debate whether Longchengornis sanyanensis is a synonym of the similar species Cathayornis yandica.
